children: , the undisputed king of artificial-intelligence accelerators, dropped approximately 1.4% to $217.76 Tuesday morning as Texas started separating real data-center projects from grid paperwork. The stakes are enormous. Electricity requests across parts of the United States now exceed 700 gigawattsmore than ten times estimated current data-center consumption.

Texas has frozen new grid connections while officials audit developers. Utilities in other markets are demanding cash upfront or proof that proposed sites are actually controlled. Nvidia's near-term machine, however, is still roaring. Its second-quarter results delivered $96.2 billion in revenue, including a staggering $89 billion from data centers. Management then guided the following quarter to approximately $108 billion.

Here is the pressure point: Nvidia is selling chips today, but the 700-gigawatt pipeline represents tomorrow's expectations. Removing fantasy projects could give investors a cleaner view of genuine AI demand. The GF Score of 95 out of 100 backs the bull case, with profitability, growth and financial strength doing the heavy lifting while valuation remains the obvious weak spot. If too much projected capacity vanishes, Nvidia's $5.3 trillion valuation could suddenly face a much tougher reality check.

title: Nvidia Slips as 700-Gigawatt Data-Center Pipeline Faces Texas Scrutiny
